name: RT-2 & Modern VLA Stack — Technical Summary
observations: SOURCE: Brohan et al., 'RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control' (Google DeepMind, arXiv:2307.15818v1, 2023). 26-page PDF read from pdf/embodied_ai_papers.

CORE IDEA: A vision-language-action (VLA) model is a pretrained VLM co-fine-tuned to emit robot actions directly. Actions are expressed as text tokens and added to the model's ordinary training targets, so no new action-specific parameters or heads are introduced — the same weights serve language, VQA and control.

ACTION TOKENIZATION (RT-2 recipe): 6-DoF end-effector delta position + delta rotation + gripper extension + a discrete 'terminate' command. Each continuous dimension is discretized into 256 uniform bins, giving an 8-integer action string, e.g. 'terminate dpos_x dpos_y dpos_z drot_x drot_y drot_z gripper'. For PaLI-X, bins map to the existing integer tokens; for PaLM-E, the 256 least-frequently-used tokens are overwritten (a form of symbol tuning).

TRAINING FORMAT: standard VQA framing — input 'Q: what action should the robot take to [instruction]? A:' plus camera image(s); target is the action token string. Loss is next-token prediction, which equals behavior cloning for the action portion.

CO-FINE-TUNING IS THE KEY ABLATION: mixing the original web VLM data with robot trajectories beats robot-only fine-tuning and beats training from scratch. Reported unseen-scenario averages: from-scratch 5B = 9; robot-only fine-tune 5B = 42, 55B = 52; co-fine-tune 5B = 44, 55B = 63. Robot data was upweighted to ~50% (PaLI-X) / ~66% (PaLM-E) of each batch; scaling model size also consistently improved generalization.

OUTPUT CONSTRAINT: when prompted with a robot-action task, decoding is restricted to the 256 valid action tokens; on ordinary vision-language prompts the full natural-language vocabulary is available.

INSTANTIATIONS: RT-2-PaLI-X (5B and 55B; ViT-22B encoder + 32B/50-layer UL2-style encoder-decoder) and RT-2-PaLM-E (12B; ViT-4B projecting into a decoder-only LLM). Trained on RT-1 robot data (13 robots, 17 months, office kitchen, 7 skills) plus web-scale VQA/captioning data.

RESULTS: ~6k real-robot evaluation trials. Seen-task success on par with RT-1 (91-93%), but unseen-condition average 62% vs 32% (RT-1) / 35% (MOO) / ~10-12% (VC-1, R3M) — roughly 2x the best baseline. Emergent skill average 60% (RT-2-PaLI-X-55B) vs 17% (RT-1), covering symbol understanding (e.g. 'move coke can near 3'), reasoning (math, logos, nutrition, color, multilingual commands), and human recognition (celebrities, 'person with glasses').

CHAIN-OF-THOUGHT: a few hundred gradient steps of fine-tuning on data augmented with a 'Plan:' field before the action tokens lets the model write a natural-language plan then the action, e.g. 'Instruction: I am hungry. Plan: pick rxbar chocolate. Action: 1 128 124 136 121 158 111 255.' This bridges VQA-style reasoning and manipulation data and enables multi-step semantic inference.

REAL-TIME INFERENCE: the 55B model runs at only 1-3 Hz, the 5B at ~5 Hz, served from a multi-TPU cloud service queried over the network and shared across robots — i.e. inference latency/frequency is the binding constraint, and decoupling the policy server from the robot is the standard mitigation.

LIMITATIONS (stated by the authors): no new physical skills are acquired from web data — only new ways of deploying existing skills; high compute cost and low control frequency; grasping specific parts, dexterous/precise motions, novel motions and deep multi-step reasoning remain failure modes; few openly fine-tunable VLMs existed at the time (they point to LLaVA as a hope).

CURRENT BEST-PRACTICE STACK (from Context7 docs): Hugging Face LeRobot (/huggingface/lerobot, v0.6.1) is the main end-to-end open framework and directly implements the VLA pattern. `lerobot-record` captures teleoperated episodes into a LeRobotDataset (multi-camera video + observation.state + action + task string, e.g. --robot.type=so101_follower, --dataset.single_task=...). `lerobot-train --policy.type=smolvla` (or pi0/pi0.5/act) fine-tunes a pretrained VLA; SmolVLA fine-tuning of lerobot/smolvla_base is ~20k steps / ~4h on one A100, with freeze_vision_encoder=True and train_expert_only=True by default, 50-step action chunks, action/state normalized mean-std and padded to max dim 32, images resized to 512x512, and a VLM backbone (vlm_model_name) plus tokenizer.

DEPLOYMENT PATTERN: LeRobot async inference mirrors RT-2's cloud-serving design — `python -m lerobot.async_inference.policy_server --host=0.0.0.0 --port=8080` on the GPU box, and `python -m lerobot.async_inference.robot_client` on the robot, tuned via actions_per_chunk (e.g. 50), chunk_size_threshold (e.g. 0.5) and an aggregation function such as weighted_average over overlapping action chunks. Action chunking is the practical answer to the 1-5 Hz problem RT-2 flagged.

MODEL LAYER: Hugging Face Transformers supplies the VLM backbones and processor plumbing (vision tower + multimodal projector + decoder-only LM; composite Processor wrapping tokenizer + image processor, e.g. PaliGemma, LLaVA, Qwen2-VL, SmolVLM2). OpenVLA-style checkpoints are consumed through the same AutoModel/AutoProcessor pattern; no dedicated OpenVLA entry was returned by the library resolver, so LeRobot was used as the authoritative VLA-workflow reference.

PRACTICAL TAKEAWAYS: (1) reuse a pretrained VLM rather than training from scratch; (2) co-train on web VLM data while fine-tuning on robot data to avoid catastrophic forgetting; (3) keep one token space for language and actions; (4) constrain decoding to valid action tokens at inference; (5) serve the policy off-robot and use action chunking to hit control rate; (6) expect semantic/generalization gains, not new motor skills.
